findings.title: Light-theme color for embedded post author links changed from 30% to 70%
findings.body: `.embedded-posts .topic-meta-data h5 a` was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`. It is now `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%))`, so the two values were swapped. Every other conversion in this PR keeps the original percentage as the light value and uses its complement for the dark value. Here light themes now render these author names much paler (70% instead of 30%). The intended value is `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`.

findings.title: Light-theme `.custom-message-length` color changed from 70% to 30%
findings.body: The original was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%)`. The replacement is `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`, so the percentages were inverted. On light mobile themes the flag-message length hint becomes much darker than before, which is an unintended regression. Desktop `modal.scss` correctly uses 70%/30% for the same selector. The mobile value should match: `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%))`.

findings.title: Mobile topic-map h3 light color changed from 20% to 50%
findings.body: `.topic-map h3` was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%)` and is now `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`. This changes the appearance on light themes, which this PR should not affect; the heading becomes noticeably lighter. The desktop counterpart correctly uses 20%/80%. The mobile value should be `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 80%))`.

findings.title: group-member-info .name light color changed from 30% to 50%
findings.body: `.group-member-info .name` was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` and is now `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`. This silently lightens member names on light themes and removes the visual distinction from `.title`, which also uses 50%. To preserve the light-theme look it should be `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`.

findings.title: Mobile group-member-info .name light color changed from 30% to 50%
findings.body: This has the same issue as the desktop file. The original was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`, and the new light-theme value is 50% with a 50% dark value. Light-theme rendering changes and member names now look the same as titles. It should be `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`.
